findings.title: Silent option drop on the `sdk` transport (index.ts:130-136).

findings.body:
**`modelUsageEntryFromWire` accepts an entry whose only token fields are invalid. This can undercount tokens.**

Lines 149-153 test `!== undefined` on the raw wire value. `usageFromWire` (Lines 95-108) tests the validated `asWireInt` result instead. The two functions disagree on what counts as "shaped".

Trigger: a `modelUsage` entry such as `{ inputTokens: -1 }`, or a fractional or string value.
1. The entry passes the shape check at Line 154.
2. Lines 156-159 map every invalid field to `0`.
3. `measureResultUsage` keeps the `modelUsage` channel and folds zeros for that model.
4. The valid flat `usage` on the same frame is never consulted as a fallback.

The header (Lines 25-27) says an invalid numeric field is "treated as absent". Under that rule this entry has no valid field. It should be unshaped, so the fold falls through to the flat channel. As written, a lying entry becomes a measured zero instead of falling back to the flat `usage`. That is the Budget.maxTokens undercount that issue #19 targets.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  const shaped =
-    rec['inputTokens'] !== undefined ||
-    rec['outputTokens'] !== undefined ||
-    rec['cacheReadInputTokens'] !== undefined ||
-    rec['cacheCreationInputTokens'] !== undefined;
-  if (!shaped) return undefined;
-  return {
-    input: asWireInt(rec['inputTokens']) ?? 0,
-    output: asWireInt(rec['outputTokens']) ?? 0,
-    cacheRead: asWireInt(rec['cacheReadInputTokens']) ?? 0,
-    cacheWrite: asWireInt(rec['cacheCreationInputTokens']) ?? 0,
-  };
+  const input = asWireInt(rec['inputTokens']);
+  const output = asWireInt(rec['outputTokens']);
+  const cacheRead = asWireInt(rec['cacheReadInputTokens']);
+  const cacheWrite = asWireInt(rec['cacheCreationInputTokens']);
+  if (
+    input === undefined &&
+    output === undefined &&
+    cacheRead === undefined &&
+    cacheWrite === undefined
+  )
+    return undefined;
+  return {
+    input: input ?? 0,
+    output: output ?? 0,
+    cacheRead: cacheRead ?? 0,
+    cacheWrite: cacheWrite ?? 0,
+  };
```
</details>

findings.body:
**Check the signal again right before `spawnImpl`, so a run cancelled during setup never starts the CLI.**

The last pre-spawn abort check is at `src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:451`. Several awaits run after that check and before the spawn:
- `store.create` / `tempWorkspace` (`src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:481-484`)
- `store.appendMessage` (`src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:488`)
- `buildManifest` (`src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:510`)
- `readCliSessionId` (`src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:529`)
- `writeMcpConfig` (`src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:536`)

If `RunOptions.signal` fires during any of these awaits, the code still spawns the CLI and writes the prompt to stdin. Only after that does the check at `src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:689` start the SIGTERM→SIGKILL ladder. During `termGraceMs`, the CLI can start its provider request. That request can spend tokens even though the caller had already cancelled.

The path instructions say: "Cancellation must actually stop client-side spend: honor the AbortSignal/cancel port". The header at `src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:17` also says an aborted signal "never dispatches".

`spawnImpl` is synchronous, and the listener attaches synchronously right after it. So a check placed directly before the spawn closes the gap. The check at `src/driver/claude-code/cli.ts:689` can stay as a backstop.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
+    // Pre-spawn recheck (I8): an abort that fired during the session/manifest/
+    // MCP-config awaits must never dispatch the CLI.
+    if (signalAborted(signal)) {
+      await removeMcpConfig(mcpConfigPath);
+      return {
+        usage: zeroUsage(),
+        usageProvenance: 'unmeasured',
+        sessionId: record.sessionId,
+        denials: [],
+        stopReason: 'aborted',
+      };
+    }
     let child: ManagedChild;
     try {
       child = this.spawnImpl({
```
</details>

As per path instructions: "Cancellation must actually stop client-side spend: honor the AbortSignal/cancel port, tear down workers and release resources on abort so no spend or process survives the run."
findings.title: Check the signal again right before `spawnImpl`, so a run cancelled during setup never starts the CLI.
A removed workspace on unbound resume makes `run()` throw an unclassified error after it has already written the prompt to the session.

findings.body:
**Settle tool handlers before returning the verdict**

If the SDK query fails while a harness call is pending, the handler can append to the session and mutate `WorkerResult.denials` after `run()` returns. Callers can therefore miss the denial. Track in-flight handlers and settle them before persisting the observation and returning the verdict.
findings.title: Settle tool handlers before returning the verdict
